title: Exam Study Planner
description: Create a structured study plan based on your subject, exam date, and current knowledge.
startingIdea: I need help preparing for an exam.
bestFor: A student who knows the subject and the exam date, and wants a plan for the days in between.
whyItWorks: This template starts with your goal, then adds context and output format. Those details help AI produce a response that's easier to use.
suggestedContext: The exam is coming up. Include the subject, the date, and what you already understand.

title: Learn a Difficult Topic
description: Get a clear explanation of a topic that is not clicking yet, starting from what you already know.
startingIdea: I want to understand a topic that is not clicking.
bestFor: Anyone studying a concept that still feels fuzzy after reading it once.
whyItWorks: Naming the topic, what you already know, and the kind of explanation you want gives the answer a place to start. You recognize the situation instead of inventing a prompt.
suggestedContext: Name the topic, what you have already tried, and the part that is confusing.

title: Create Practice Questions
description: Make practice questions that match what you are studying and show you how to check your answers.
startingIdea: I want practice questions for something I am learning.
bestFor: A student who wants to test recall before an exam or assignment.
whyItWorks: A goal, the topic, and a requested format turn a vague wish for practice into questions you can actually answer.
suggestedContext: Name the subject, the chapters or skills to cover, and how hard the questions should be.

title: Resume Improvement
description: Strengthen a resume for a specific role by clarifying the experience you want to highlight.
startingIdea: I want help improving my resume.
bestFor: Someone applying for a role and unsure which experience to lead with.
whyItWorks: The role, the reader, and the kind of revision you want are easier to point at than to remember as prompt rules.
suggestedContext: Name the role, the parts of your experience that matter most, and what feels weak right now.

title: Interview Preparation
description: Prepare for an interview with questions, stories from your experience, and a way to practice answers.
startingIdea: I have an interview coming up and I want to prepare.
bestFor: A candidate who knows the role and wants to practice how they will talk about their work.
whyItWorks: The company, the role, and the answer format give the practice a real audience instead of a generic list of interview tips.
suggestedContext: Name the role, the kind of interview, and the experiences you want to draw on.

title: Professional Email
description: Draft a clear work email when you know the person, the point, and what you need back.
startingIdea: I need to write a professional email.
bestFor: Someone writing to a manager, client, or colleague about a specific request.
whyItWorks: Who it is for, why you are writing, and how the reply should look keep the email short and usable.
suggestedContext: Name the recipient, the situation, and what you want them to do after reading.

title: Explain Code
description: Explain a snippet, including Python, in plain language without assuming you know the syntax.
startingIdea: I want this code explained in plain language.
bestFor: A learner reading code they did not write and want to follow what it does.
whyItWorks: The language, the snippet, and the audience tell the explanation how much detail to include.
suggestedContext: Paste the code or describe it, and say which language it is, such as Python.

title: Debug a Problem
description: Work through a bug by naming what you expected, what happened, and what you have already tried.
startingIdea: Something in my code is not working and I want to debug it.
bestFor: Someone stuck on an error who wants a next step, not a lecture.
whyItWorks: Expected behavior, the actual result, and the output format turn a stuck feeling into a problem that can be traced.
suggestedContext: Describe what you expected, what happened instead, and any error message you can share.

title: Learn a Programming Concept
description: Learn one programming idea, such as Python functions, with a small example you can reuse.
startingIdea: I want to learn a programming concept, such as Python functions.
bestFor: A beginner who wants one concept explained with an example, not a whole course.
whyItWorks: One concept, your current level, and a requested example keep the answer inside what you can use today.
suggestedContext: Name the concept, the language, and what you already understand.

title: Improve an Essay
description: Revise an essay so the argument, structure, and audience are easier for a reader to follow.
startingIdea: I want to improve an essay I have already started.
bestFor: A writer who has a draft and wants help with clarity, not a new topic.
whyItWorks: The assignment, the reader, and the kind of revision you want keep the feedback attached to your draft.
suggestedContext: Say what the essay is for, who will read it, and which part feels weakest.

title: Write a Professional Email
description: Shape a professional email from a rough note so the request is easy to answer.
startingIdea: I want to turn a rough note into a professional email.
bestFor: Someone who knows what they need to say and wants the wording to sound clear.
whyItWorks: A recipient, a purpose, and a short finished email are easier to recognize than a blank page of etiquette rules.
suggestedContext: Include the rough note, who will read it, and the outcome you want.

title: Prepare a Presentation
description: Outline a presentation for a specific audience, with a clear point and a structure you can speak from.
startingIdea: I need to prepare a presentation.
bestFor: Someone who knows the topic and the room, and needs a structure before making slides.
whyItWorks: The audience, the time you have, and the output shape give the outline a job. You do not have to remember how a presentation prompt should look.
suggestedContext: Name the topic, who will be in the room, and how long you have to speak.

title: Research Topic Breakdown
description: Break a research topic into questions, sources to look for, and a sensible order of work.
startingIdea: I want a research topic broken into parts I can actually study.
bestFor: A student or researcher starting a topic that still feels too broad.
whyItWorks: The question, the field, and a structured output keep the research from turning into a pile of links.
suggestedContext: Name the topic, the course or field, and what you already know.

title: Compare Research Ideas
description: Compare two research ideas so you can see the question, the effort, and which one fits your goal.
startingIdea: I want to compare two research ideas before I commit to one.
bestFor: Someone choosing between topics and wanting a fair comparison, not a verdict from nowhere.
whyItWorks: Putting both ideas, the decision you need to make, and a comparison format in one place makes the tradeoff visible.
suggestedContext: Describe both ideas, the deadline, and what would make one of them a better fit.

title: Weekly Planning
description: Turn the week ahead into a plan that fits your priorities, time, and energy.
startingIdea: I want a plan for the week ahead.
bestFor: Someone with a list of tasks who wants the week to have an order.
whyItWorks: Your priorities, the time you actually have, and a checklist format make the plan something you can follow.
suggestedContext: List the commitments you already have and the few outcomes that matter most.

title: Meeting Action Items
description: Pull owners, deadlines, and next steps out of meeting notes.
startingIdea: I need the action items from a meeting.
bestFor: Someone leaving a meeting with notes and wanting a list people can act on.
whyItWorks: The notes, the people involved, and a checklist ask for decisions instead of another summary of the conversation.
suggestedContext: Paste the notes or describe the decisions, and name anyone who owns a next step.

title: Brainstorm Ideas
description: Explore a range of ideas for a project, then narrow them with the constraints you already know.
startingIdea: I want help brainstorming ideas.
bestFor: Someone at the start of a project who wants options before choosing a direction.
whyItWorks: The project, who it is for, and a list format give the brainstorm a boundary so the ideas stay usable.
suggestedContext: Describe the project, who it is for, and any limits you already know.

title: Content Ideas
description: Find content ideas that fit a topic, an audience, and the format you actually publish in.
startingIdea: I want content ideas for something I am making.
bestFor: A creator who knows the subject and the channel, and wants ideas they can produce.
whyItWorks: Audience, topic, and format are the details people can recognize. Together they keep ideas from drifting into anything.
suggestedContext: Name the topic, where it will be published, and who you hope will read or watch it.

title: Explain a Dataset
description: Explain what a dataset contains, which columns matter, and what a beginner should notice first.
startingIdea: I want a dataset explained before I analyze it.
bestFor: Someone opening a table or spreadsheet and wanting to know what they are looking at.
whyItWorks: The columns, the question you care about, and a plain explanation make the dataset readable before any analysis starts.
suggestedContext: Describe the dataset, the important columns, and what you hope to understand.

title: Analyze Data
description: Look at data for a specific question and come back with findings you can check.
startingIdea: I want help analyzing data I already have.
bestFor: Someone with a table and a question, who wants findings rather than a generic chart.
whyItWorks: The question, the data you have, and the format of the answer keep the analysis tied to a decision.
suggestedContext: Describe the data, the question you need answered, and any comparison that matters.
